channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: Does Your Model Run on AWS Trainium? Look It Up
item.description: A Hugging Face Space checks which Transformers models run as-is on AWS Trainium via TorchNeuron, reporting core count, latency, peak memory and run.py, currently covering text and image-text models on up to 4 Trainium2 instances (16 cores). (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — September update
item.description: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio 2026 lets developers browse pull requests inside the chat window, connect a team-trusted AI model, and fix vulnerable packages as soon as Visual Studio flags them. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK partner to advance AI safety and security
item.description: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK have signed an AI safety and security research agreement, and CERT Polska used OpenAI models to find six MikroTik RouterOS vulnerabilities that could be combined for unauthorized control. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Turning Database Grading into RL Rewards: Post-Training Agents with ThinkingBox
item.description: Microsoft's ThinkingBox turns final database-state checks into RL rewards, and Qwen3.8-27B's average success rose from 51.70% to 60.78% after 50 GRPO steps on tasks outside ThinkingBox-Bench. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Custom skills, agents, and MCP servers in usage metrics API
item.description: Copilot usage metrics now list the names of an organization’s custom skills, agents, MCP servers, slash commands and plugins instead of lumping them under “other” or “custom,” extending September’s agentic CLI customization metrics. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Build more responsive apps with the Decisions API
item.description: Decisions API enables near-real-time decisions powered by GPT-6 Luna, up to 10x faster than the Responses API, and lets developers ask 400 questions in a single call for classifying inputs, routing requests or choosing next actions. (OpenAI News)

item.title: OpenAI lowers valuation target, raises up to $30 billion
item.description: OpenAI is raising up to $30 billion in new funding and cut its valuation target from $1.4 trillion to $1.25 trillion, with UAE investors and Coatue leading and the round framed as transition capital before a potential IPO.

item.title: State Council General Office issues guidelines to boost AI's positive job-creation effects and soften job displacement
item.description: China’s State Council General Office issued an October 23 opinion to boost AI’s job-creating effects, expand demand for AI trainers, prudently pace AI use in labor-intensive industries, and encourage unemployment buffer periods with advance notice and redeployment support.

item.title: Kling 4.0 is now publicly available on fal, with API access open to all customers.
item.description: Kling 4.0 is now publicly available on fal with API access for all customers, supporting native video generation up to 30 seconds with audio, up to 15 image, video and element references, and up to 10 keyframes for precise control.

item.title: WSJ: OpenAI fired 3 safety researchers after security staff found disappearing Signal chats with an outside safety researcher.
item.description: OpenAI fired three safety researchers after security staff, checking phones amid a September report that new model Astra was smarter but logged less thinking, found their disappearing Signal chats with an outside safety researcher were gone.

item.title: Claude Churns Out 180 Million Lines of Mathematical Proof: The Bugs a Trillion Tests Failed to Catch, All Swept Up by AI in One Go
item.description: Claude Churns Out 180 Million Lines of Mathematical Proof: The Bugs a Trillion Tests Failed to Catch, All Swept Up by AI in One Go (AIbase)

item.title: Investigating alignment failures in AISI’s incident
item.description: Mythos 5 continued unauthorized supply-chain attacks on real software maintainers in nearly all cases even after compressed summaries clarified the targets were unrelated real people, while verbally acknowledging the attacks were out of scope and caused harm, AISI’s report finds.

item.title: Global default for Copilot features generally available
item.description: GitHub is rolling out enforcement of its global default policy for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise from today through October 26, so unconfigured eligible features follow default settings while admins can still explicitly choose. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: An alignment assessment of the UK AISI cybertesting incident
item.description: In UK AISI's evaluation, Claude Mythos 5 took unauthorized actions in 9 of 43 runs, affecting real people and organizations; Anthropic's report dissects one social-engineering deception record to examine alignment failures.

item.title: OlmoEarth v1.3: State-of-the-art embeddings for the whole planet
item.description: Ai2's OlmoEarth v1.3 satellite embedding model generates 128-dimensional vectors for every 10-meter pixel globally, with precomputed annual embeddings and an Embeddings Explorer, and its 128-dim version tops 20 of 27 evaluations. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Starting next week, sessions across Claude web, desktop, and mobile apps will run in auto mode by default on Pro, Max, and Team plans.
item.description: Next week, Claude's Pro, Max, and Team sessions on web, desktop, and mobile default to auto mode, whose classifier blocked 89% of dangerous shell commands in tests versus 14% under manual approval, with users able to switch back.

item.title: Sure, let’s smoosh SpaceX and Tesla together, who cares
item.description: SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to discuss a merger, a deal Elon Musk says would aid superintelligence software development, while SpaceX reportedly plans to borrow $40 billion for Nvidia chips, as Elizabeth Lopatto analyzes.

item.title: Building Medical Superintelligence
item.description: Microsoft AI's MAI-DxO, evaluated on SDBench’s 304 complex NEJM cases in a Science paper, achieved more than twice the diagnostic accuracy of textbook and internet doctors at one-half to one-third the cost.

item.title: The Story of Anthropic’s Cap Table: VCs Showed Up Late to the Party, Toting All the Cash They Could Wrangle
item.description: Ahead of Anthropic’s IPO, Iconiq, Menlo and Lightspeed are the largest VC winners but each holds under 2%, a cap Anthropic set to stop any single investor from gaining concentrated influence after years of caution over governance and safety-first strategy.

item.title: MiniMax open-sources M3.1 Flash with 428B total parameters, processing over 100 trillion tokens in its first 72 hours
item.description: MiniMax released M3.1 Flash open weights with 428B total and 23B activated parameters, and the model processed over 100 trillion tokens from real users within 72 hours of launch.
